solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Close game, after changeover, ending in terrible weather

parts.note: a close is a finish or conclusion, an end

indicators.note: after a changeover the two letters swap places, so the game's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, the game

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its final letter, here of 'terrible'

explanation.surface: A sports report: a tight match finishing, after the teams change ends, in dreadful conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb, as in weathering a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather hardship is to survive or withstand it without giving way.

clue.text: Entertained parts of Einstein's theory, with rereads periodically

parts.note: Einstein's theory E=mc squared contains the letters E, M and C, ignoring the equals sign and the power

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here the even ones of 'rereads'

explanation.surface: A student goes over Einstein's relativity again and again, reading it in sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from MC, master of ceremonies: to compere a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as master of ceremonies is to host and entertain an audience as compere.

clue.text: Insect trail on sole inhibits foot

parts.note: to trail something is to drag it along behind you

indicators.note: to inhibit is to restrain or hold in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: An insect drags itself along with a damaged sole that stops its foot working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just joins the first piece to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-bodied, four-winged insect hunts over ponds; it is a straightforward example of an insect.

clue.text: Novel features latterly in Spectator magazine Boris harangued

indicators.note: the latter features of the two words are their closing letters
a harangue is a loud public speech, so the name is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Boris Becker is the German tennis champion; his surname is the word spoken

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, once editor of The Spectator, ranting in its pages about a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson edited The Spectator, but this Boris is the tennis player Becker. The sound match is loose, as the blogger notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1938 gothic book of this title is a famous English novel.

clue.text: Medium embodies such a psychic state

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes
embodies is read as 'is', as in 'she is courage itself'
such means so, as in 'such a/so great'
Uri Geller is the famous spoon-bending self-proclaimed psychic

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium embodies a psychic trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' and 'psychic' work together in the surface but are separate pieces; 'state' is a US state, not a frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, nicknamed the Show-Me State, on the Mississippi.

clue.text: My word is final in Canada, Yankee

indicators.note: the final letter in 'Canada' is used

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the last word in Canada belongs to the Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, the old-fashioned 'Gosh!' or 'Well I never!'.

clue.text: Cod 'n' chips requires a vegetable

indicators.note: cod means fake or mock, so the letters given are a sham version to rearrange

parts.note: 'n' is the clipped form of 'and', giving N

explanation.surface: A fish supper order: cod and chips, plus something green on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish but is the adjective meaning fake, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy green, beloved of Popeye, is a common vegetable.

clue.text: American paired to avoid Democratic general

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep out of its way, so the letter is removed

parts.note: dual means paired or twofold, as in dual controls
D is the abbreviation for Democratic, the US party

explanation.surface: An American politician teamed up with someone to dodge a Democratic general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is not a military officer but an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: General and normal both describe what is customary or widespread, the everyday case.

clue.text: Faultless pub once abandoned 'Time'

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the word's letters run loose

explanation.surface: A blameless pub that once gave up calling last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a pub stopping 'Time!' at closing; 'abandoned' signals a rearrangement of ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guiltless or blameless is free of fault.

clue.text: Crustacean-like starters in Chinese restaurant served with salt in reserve

indicators.note: the starters of the two words are their first letters

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman
by means in reserve, as in 'standing by' or 'put by'

explanation.surface: A Chinese restaurant review: crab starters served with salt kept on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' and 'salt' read as menu items; one picks first letters, the other is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective formed from the creature name literally means resembling the shellfish, alongside its usual sense of grumpy.

clue.text: Buttoned-up old historian briefly outside in rain

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian

indicators.note: the outside letters in 'rain' are its first and last

explanation.surface: An old historian, buttoned up in a coat, stands briefly outside in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone buttoned-up keeps their thoughts to themselves: reserved and saying little.

clue.text: Barnet prone to sporadic clamping foremost in centre

indicators.note: the letter goes in the centre of the rearranged letters
sporadic means scattered irregularly, so these letters are scattered into a new order
the foremost letter of 'clamping' is its first

explanation.surface: A North London suburb is prone to occasional wheel-clamping in its town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but in Cockney rhyming slang Barnet (Fair) means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short, sleek 1920s women's hairstyle, and Barnet is rhyming slang for hair.

clue.text: Ambassador, in NATO building, ready for congress

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE

explanation.surface: An ambassador at NATO headquarters gets ready for a congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' suggests a political meeting but means sexual union here.
explanation.definitionFit: A female animal in season is receptive to mating, which is what congress means here.

clue.text: Herb moved cigar boxes closer to smell

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
moved means shifted around, so these letters change places
the closer of a word is its last letter, here of 'smell'

explanation.surface: A herb shifted the cigar boxes nearer, to smell them.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent bulb is used as a herb or seasoning in cooking.

clue.text: Motor, its outer bearings replaced by amateurs, causes complaint

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for amateur, so two amateurs give two As

indicators.note: bearings are compass points, here E for east at each end of the word, swapped for other letters

parts.note: an engine is a motor
A is an abbreviation for amateur, so two amateurs give two As

explanation.surface: A motor whose outer bearings were replaced by amateurs causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearings' looks mechanical but means compass points: both outer letters are E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: This chest pain from poor blood supply to the heart is a medical complaint.

clue.text: Cleaner around toilet having brief success

definitions.meaning: Flash is a brand of household cleaner in the UK, and the pan is the toilet bowl, so it is the cleaner at work in the bowl
an early showy triumph that comes to nothing, from an old flintlock gun's powder flaring without firing

explanation.surface: Bathroom cleaning product advertising itself, with a fleeting triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a short-lived success that fails to last, like a gun's powder flaring without firing.

clue.text: Conservationists with green wellies finally enter favourite festival

indicators.note: the pieces enter the other word, going inside it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
NT is the National Trust, the British conservation charity
eco means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of 'wellies'

explanation.surface: Eco-campaigners in green wellington boots turn up at a favourite festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellies are wellington boots, the rubber boots British festival-goers wear in mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, is a church festival.

clue.text: Classical great, during bow, given this bottle of booze?

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc
magna is Latin for great, as in Magna Carta

explanation.surface: A grand classical figure takes a bow and is handed a bottle of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: This brandy from Gascony is a spirit sold by the bottle, so a bottle of it is booze.

clue.text: Palace boss abruptly charged a player, then retracted — it's nothing for millionaire, ultimately

indicators.note: one letter stands in for the other, a replacement
retracted means drawn back, so everything so far is read backwards

parts.note: the boss is No. 1, written NO I

indicators.note: abruptly means cut off suddenly, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a charged wire is live
taken as written, a player

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of 'millionaire'

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A palace chief suddenly charged a footballer, then withdrew: small change for a millionaire.
explanation.walkthrough: Retracting NOILIVAPLAYER gives REYALPAVILION; then O ('nothing') replaces the E. The Royal Pavilion is the Regency palace in Brighton, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: George IV's Indian-style seaside residence in Brighton is a royal palace.

clue.text: Habit of medics to throw up a lot, taking in the basics

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so the other piece goes inside
to throw something up is to toss it in the air, scattering the letters

parts.note: the ABC of a subject is its basics

explanation.surface: Doctors' habit of vomiting a great deal, while learning the fundamentals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is a garment, as in a nun's habit, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors and lab staff wear this white coat, a sort of working uniform or garment.

clue.text: Such style cut by Brando, from the heart, for character of Godfather

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: italic is a style of type; in the original clue this was printed in italics

indicators.note: from the heart means the central letters of 'Brando'

explanation.surface: Marlon Brando's heartfelt acting style, used to play the Godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such style' relies on the words being printed in italics, which the newspaper missed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godfather's Corleone family is Sicilian, so the nationality is the character's.

clue.text: Couple check underneath Italian bread, discarding half

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits underneath the other
half of the bread's letters, the first four, are thrown away

parts.note: ciabatta is a flat Italian bread
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Two people inspect what's under some Italian bread, throwing half of it away.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or fasten them together, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Low life periodically harm old Lincoln convertible

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of 'harm'
convertible means able to be changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: Lowlifes now and then damage an old Lincoln convertible car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low life' is not criminals but a simple single-celled organism, low on the scale of life.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism is about as primitive a life form as there is.

clue.text: Cop bust around centre of Hastings — one's put behind bars

indicators.note: the broken letters go around the other piece
bust means broken, so these letters are broken up
the centre of 'Hastings' is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A policeman makes an arrest in central Hastings, a seaside town; someone is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests prison, but it is a pub bar where spirit measures hang behind the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's spirit dispenser fixed to an upturned bottle is mounted behind the bar.

clue.text: Soldier eager to ditch latest tense bird

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: ditching the latest letter means dropping the last one

parts.note: keen means eager
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A soldier keen to get rid of the newest nervous recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This small long-tailed parrot is a bird.

clue.text: Couple (Viennese) embraced for one of Strauss's

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the answer is held inside the words

explanation.surface: A Viennese couple waltz in each other's arms to Strauss.
explanation.walkthrough: Strauss suggests the Viennese waltz composers, but this is Levi Strauss, the jeans maker; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeans made by Levi Strauss's company are called by the founder's first name.

clue.text: Gas money, that's remitted, little man held back for example

indicators.note: remitted is read as sent back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: held means contained, so one piece is inside the other

parts.note: Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Money for gas being sent back, with a little man kept waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourless element makes up most of the air we breathe, a gas.

clue.text: Plant drawn very minute in plan

indicators.note: drawn means pulled back, so the whole is read in reverse
the two pieces go in the other word

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A plant drawn in minute detail in a garden plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests sketching; Chambers gives 'pulled back' as a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This acacia with fluffy yellow flowers, and its sensitive cousin, are plants.

clue.text: Business, changing tack, starts to import lucrative drink

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters change order
the starts to the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A firm changes direction and begins to import a profitable drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed alcoholic drink such as a martini is a cocktail.

clue.text: Susan vacated long grass

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of 'Susan' remain

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Susan has left the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not a plant but the verb to inform on someone, and 'long' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on criminals is British slang for informing to the police.
